artiest/kabza-de-small-en-dj-maphorisa.text:
Kabza De Small and DJ Maphorisa are two South African DJs and producers who became known as a duo through amapiano, a South African style of house. Kabza De Small is regarded as one of the faces of the genre. DJ Maphorisa, born Themba Sekowe in 1987 in Soshanguve, is of Tsonga and Lobedu descent. His stage name means 'the police' in Tsonga. He first signed with Kalawa Jazmee Records and later started his own label, BlaqBoy Music.

Maphorisa built his name as a producer of hits for artists from many genres, such as Uhuru with Y-Tjukuta, Kwesta with Ngud', Busiswa with Lahla and Shekinah with Suited. In his work he blends house, gqom, amapiano and Afropop. Among others, he has worked with Wizkid, Drake, Black Coffee and Major Lazer. His single Midnight Starring, with Moonchild Sanelly, DJ Tira and Busiswa, appeared in 2018. In 2021 he made the album Rumble in the Jungle with Kabza De Small and TRESOR, and in the same year the song Abalele with Ami Faku. In Lagos he won the award for African DJ of the Year.

Amapiano has a relaxed but danceable groove, with deep bass loops, jazzy piano chords and a drum pattern that belongs to house. From 2019 onwards the genre spread from the South African townships across Africa and the world. The duo represent that wave and show how a local style can become popular worldwide.
artiest/kabza-de-small-en-dj-maphorisa.listen: Listen to Asibe Happy and notice the low bass loop and the loose piano chords: how does that relaxed groove keep you moving all the same, and when does the vocal come in?

artiest/kaija-saariaho.text: Kaija Saariaho, from Helsinki, studied in Freiburg and settled in Paris in 1982, where she analysed sound with computers at IRCAM. Working from spectralism, she wrote music in which timbre plays the leading role and instruments and electronics flow into one another. Her first opera, L'Amour de loin from 2000, is about a troubadour who falls in love with a woman he has never seen. In 2016 it became the first opera by a woman to be staged at the Metropolitan Opera since 1903.
artiest/kaija-saariaho.listen: Listen to the Traversée from L'Amour de loin and hear how the orchestra paints the sea with rippling, glittering layers of sound.

artiest/kaluli-zangers-koluba-groep.text:
The Kaluli are a people of the rainforest of Papua New Guinea, around Mount Bosavi in the Southern Highlands. The Kaluli singers of the Koluba group are not professional performers, but men and women from a village community who sang while they worked in and around the forest. Nothing about the individual singers has been recorded in the available sources, so this text sticks to what is generally known. The 1991 recording Cutting Trees for a Garden is a field recording.

For the Kaluli, music is bound up with the nature around them. Birds, water and insects have a place in their songs and in their conception of sound. Many songs are about paths, rivers and places in the forest, and are sung to remember, to mourn or to celebrate. Work songs accompany tasks such as cutting trees for a garden, where song and labour coincide.

The singing is often polyphonic, with voices that overlap and alternate, without a conductor and without a fixed metre. The recordings let you hear how singing and surroundings flow into one another, with the sound of the forest in the background. For the history of pop, this kind of music matters because it shows that music is not always a separate performance but part of daily life, and because such field recordings have later inspired composers and producers.
artiest/kaluli-zangers-koluba-groep.listen: Listen to Cutting Trees for a Garden and pay attention to the surroundings: besides the voices, can you hear sounds of the forest, and how the singers let their voices overlap?

artiest/kamasi-washington.text: Tenor saxophonist Kamasi Washington grew up in Los Angeles, where his father was a saxophonist and music teacher. As a teenager he played with Thundercat and Ronald Bruner Jr. in a group that was later called The West Coast Get Down. He played with Snoop Dogg and Lauryn Hill, and played and arranged on Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp a Butterfly. In 2015 he released The Epic on Brainfeeder, an album of nearly three hours with big band, choir and strings. John Coltrane and Pharoah Sanders are his clear models. Washington brought a new, young audience to jazz.
artiest/kamasi-washington.listen: Hear how choir, strings and saxophone together build a spiritual climax.

artiest/kan-ami.text:
Kan'ami Kiyotsugu was a Japanese Noh actor, writer and musician of the Muromachi period. He was born in 1333 in Iga Province as Yūzaki Kiyotsugu and died in 1384 in Suruga Province. He is the father of the famous playwright Zeami Motokiyo. His name occurs in several forms, such as Kanze Kiyotsugu.

His career began in Obata in the Kansai region, where he founded a sarugaku troupe. The troupe moved to Yamato and became the Yuzaki troupe, which would become the basis of Noh theatre. He grew ever more popular and travelled to Kyoto to perform. In 1374 the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu was in the audience. He was so impressed that he became Kan'ami's patron. That brought the troupe into high circles.

Kan'ami was the first writer to work the kusemai style of singing and dancing into his plays, together with dengaku dances from rural harvest festivals. In this way he blended popular elements with the court audience. He trained his son Zeami in his style, and Zeami eventually succeeded him as head of the Kanze school of Noh. In this way Kan'ami laid the foundation for a form of theatre with song, dance and music that is still performed today, and that is also important for the music history of Japan.
artiest/kan-ami.listen: Listen to a recording of Noh music. Notice the flute, the drums and the long, almost spoken singing, and how the silences between the sounds are just as important as the sounds themselves.

artiest/kanda-bongo-man.text:
Kanda Bongo Man, born Bongo Kanda in 1955, is a Congolese soukous singer. His career began in 1973, when he became the singer of the band Belle Mambo. His sound was influenced there by Tabu Ley. In 1979 he moved to Paris, where his solo career took off and his music took in elements of zouk, which had been popularised by Kassav from the French Antilles. His first solo albums, Iyole in 1981 and Djessy in 1982, were hits.

He is known for a structural innovation in soukous. Previously, a number of verses were sung with a single guitar solo at the end. Kanda Bongo Man had a guitar solo played after every verse, sometimes even at the start of the song. His form of soukous led to the rhythmic dance kwassa kwassa, in which the hips move back and forth while the hands follow the hips.

Like many African rumba and soukous musicians, he had a following of musicians, many of whom later became soloists themselves. The best known is Diblo Dibala, nicknamed Machine Gun, who played guitar on several albums, including Kwasa Kwasa and Amour Fou. Kanda Bongo Man still tours in Europe and the United States. In 2005 he performed at Live 8: Africa Calling in Cornwall, and he often played at the Africa Oyé Festival in Liverpool. His music brought the light, danceable Congolese guitar style to a worldwide audience.
artiest/kanda-bongo-man.listen: Listen to Sai and pay attention to the guitar: how do the vocal parts and guitar solos alternate, and how does the fast rhythm keep the dancing going?

artiest/kansas-joe-mccoy.text:
Kansas Joe McCoy, in full Wilbur Joe McCoy, was an American singer, guitarist and songwriter in the Delta blues. He was born in 1905 in Raymond, Mississippi, and was the older brother of the blues accompanist Papa Charlie McCoy. As a young man he was drawn by the music scene of Memphis, where in the 1920s he played guitar and sang. There he formed a duo with his later wife, the guitarist Lizzie Douglas, better known as Memphis Minnie. Their 1930 recording of Bumble Bee for Columbia Records became a hit. That same year they moved to Chicago, where they were an important part of the emerging blues scene.

After their divorce he formed the Harlem Hamfats together with his brother. In 1936 that band recorded The Weed Smoker's Dream. McCoy later reworked the song, changed the lyrics and gave it the title Why Don't You Do Right?. Lil Green recorded it in 1941, and a year later Benny Goodman and Peggy Lee made a version of it, with which Lee scored her first hit. It remains a jazz standard and is his most enduring composition. In the 1940s he led the band Big Joe and his Rhythm, with Robert Nighthawk on harmonica, among others. He died in 1950 in Chicago, aged 44.

His influence extends to rock. Robert Plant played Jimmy Page a recording of When the Levee Breaks by McCoy and Memphis Minnie, after which Led Zeppelin recorded the song for Led Zeppelin IV (1971). Neither of them was credited on the first release, though Minnie later received recognition.
artiest/kansas-joe-mccoy.listen: Listen to When the Levee Breaks by Kansas Joe McCoy and Memphis Minnie. Notice how two guitars complement each other and how narrative the singing is. Then compare it with the Led Zeppelin version.

artiest/kanye-west.text:
Kanye West is an American rapper, singer, songwriter and producer from Chicago. He started as a producer behind the scenes before stepping up to the microphone himself. His debut album The College Dropout was released in 2004 and was an immediate big success. It was followed by Late Registration (2005) and Graduation (2007), both of which entered the American album chart at number one.

In 2008 he took a different path. On 808s & Heartbreak he hardly rapped at all: he sang, in a voice distorted by Auto-Tune, about loss and a failed relationship. He built the beats around the Roland TR-808, the drum machine from the 1980s that already had a long history in hip hop. The album was cool, bare and sombre, and many younger artists later adopted that atmosphere. West then made My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy (2010), Watch the Throne (2011) with Jay-Z, Yeezus (2013) and The Life of Pablo (2016). That last album was the first to top the Billboard 200 mainly thanks to streaming. Later releases included Ye (2018), Jesus Is King (2019) and Donda (2021).

West is one of the producers who have changed the sound of hip hop the most in the twenty-first century. He combined samples, synthesizers and sung melodies, and showed that a rapper could also sound vulnerable and doubtful. 808s & Heartbreak is regarded as a turning point: after that record, singing with Auto-Tune became completely normal in hip hop.
artiest/kanye-west.listen: Listen to Love Lockdown and notice the bare construction: a heavy, dry drum part and a few piano chords, with the Auto-Tuned vocal above them. Hear how the drums come in much louder and fuller later in the song.

artiest/karat.text:
Karat is a German rock band that was formed in 1975 in East Berlin, in the GDR. The band grew out of the jazz-rock group Panta Rhei. Keyboardist and composer Ulrich Ed Swillms and guitarist Herbert Dreilich both played in it. After singer Hans-Joachim Neumann went into military service in 1977, Dreilich became the only singer, and his voice became the group's trademark. The first album, Karat (1978), contained the hit König der Welt.

The breakthrough came with Über sieben Brücken (1979). The title song, Über sieben Brücken musst du gehn, is still the band's best-known song. The song Albatros on the same record had a double meaning: the albatross knows no borders, and listeners could read that as criticism of the travel restrictions and the Wall. When the West German singer Peter Maffay recorded the song in 1980, it also became a big hit in the West. Der blaue Planet (1982), with a title song about the threat of nuclear war and environmental disasters, became the best-selling album ever made by an East German artist. Karat was the only GDR band to appear on the West German television programme Wetten, dass..?.

Karat's music is melodic progressive rock with a lot of keyboards, philosophical German lyrics and long, building songs. After the fall of the Wall, many East German fans chose Western records and the band briefly dropped out of view. Herbert Dreilich died in 2004; his son Claudius took his place. Karat shows how rock musicians in the GDR managed to say something within the limits of censorship.
artiest/karat.listen: Listen to Über sieben Brücken musst du gehn and notice how Ed Swillms's keyboards and Herbert Dreilich's voice together set the mood. Then put Peter Maffay's version next to it and hear what changes when a West German singer takes the song over.

artiest/karina-canellakis.text:
Karina Canellakis is an American conductor and violinist, born in 1981 in New York. She has a Greek and Russian background and grew up in a musical family. Her father Martin became a conductor, her mother Sheryl a pianist. She studied violin at the Curtis Institute and from 2005 to 2007 played in the Orchester-Akademie of the Berliner Philharmoniker. There Simon Rattle encouraged her interest in conducting. She then studied conducting at the Juilliard School, with Alan Gilbert among others.

In 2014 she became assistant conductor of the Dallas Symphony Orchestra. She made her European debut in 2015 with the Chamber Orchestra of Europe, as a last-minute replacement for Nikolaus Harnoncourt. In 2016 she won the Georg Solti Conducting Award. In 2018 she became chief conductor of the Radio Filharmonisch Orkest in the Netherlands, the first woman in that post at a Dutch orchestra. In 2018 she conducted the Nobel Prize Concert in Stockholm, and in 2019 she became the first woman to lead the First Night of the Proms. Later she also became principal guest conductor of the Rundfunk-Sinfonieorchester Berlin and first guest conductor of the London Philharmonic Orchestra.

Her recordings include Beethoven (2023), the Concerto for Orchestra (2023) and Duke Bluebeard's Castle (2025). Her career shows that one of the most important conducting posts in classical music is no longer reserved for men alone. She lives with her family in the Netherlands.
artiest/karina-canellakis.listen: Listen to a movement from her recording of the Concerto for Orchestra. Notice how the orchestral sections pass the melody to one another and how precisely the conductor makes the transitions coincide.

artiest/karl-bohm.text:
Karl Böhm was an Austrian conductor, born in 1894 in Graz and died in 1981 in Salzburg. He was the son of a lawyer and first studied law. He then went to the conservatoire, also in Vienna. In 1917 he made his debut as a conductor in Graz. Via the opera houses of Munich, Darmstadt and Hamburg he came to Dresden in 1934, where he headed the Semperoper until 1942. There he conducted the first performances of Richard Strauss's Die schweigsame Frau (1935) and Daphne (1938). Daphne is dedicated to him. From 1943 he worked at the Vienna State Opera, where he later became music director.

After the war came a two-year ban under denazification. He then conducted again in Milan, Paris and Buenos Aires. In 1957 he made his debut at the Metropolitan Opera in New York, where he conducted 262 performances. From 1962 he appeared at Bayreuth. His Wagner received mixed reviews. At the end of his life he worked with the London Symphony Orchestra, of which he became president.

Böhm is known for his sturdy, rhythmic performances of Mozart. In the 1960s he recorded all of Mozart's symphonies with the Berliner Philharmoniker. His recordings of Beethoven's symphonies with the Wiener Philharmoniker from 1971 were highly regarded. He also championed Alban Berg's Wozzeck and Lulu, when they were not yet part of the standard repertoire. In this way he represents the generation of conductors who recorded the great operas on disc.
artiest/karl-bohm.listen: Listen to the beginning of Beethoven's Eroica in his 1962 recording. Notice how firm and regular the rhythm remains, even when the orchestra gets louder.

artiest/karlheinz-stockhausen.text: Karlheinz Stockhausen studied in Cologne and with Messiaen in Paris, and from 1953 worked in the electronic studio of the broadcaster WDR in Cologne. He was one of the first to forge electronic sounds and recorded voices into a single composition. In Gesang der Jünglinge from 1956, the voice of a boy fuses with electronic tones that move through space. His ideas also inspired pop musicians, and his portrait appears on the cover of The Beatles' Sgt. Pepper.
artiest/karlheinz-stockhausen.listen: Listen to Gesang der Jünglinge and hear how the boy's voice is sometimes intelligible and sometimes dissolves into electronic sounds, short clicks and noise.

artiest/kassia.text:
Kassia, also spelled Kassiani, was a Byzantine Greek composer, hymnographer and poet. She lived from about 810 to 865 and is regarded as the only known woman whose music is heard in the Byzantine liturgy. She was born in Constantinople into a wealthy family and was known for being exceptionally beautiful and intelligent. Later she became abbess of a convent in the west of the city.

About fifty hymns by her have survived, mainly stichera, short sung texts for church services. For at least twenty-six of them it is uncertain whether they are really hers, because many hymns are anonymous or are attributed to different writers in different manuscripts. In addition, at least 261 epigrams and maxims are attributed to her. The oldest manuscripts of her work are centuries younger than her own life, as is the case with her predecessors Romanos the Melodist and Andrew of Crete.

A well-known story tells that she took part in a bride show, by which Byzantine princes sometimes chose a wife. The young emperor Theophilos told her that evil came through a woman. Kassia replied that the better things came through a woman too. He then rejected her and chose Theodora. Kassia is one of the few women of the medieval Byzantine period who wrote under their own name. In that way she is a rare early female voice in the history of Western music.
artiest/kassia.listen: Listen to a recording of a hymn by Kassia. Notice the long, unaccompanied single-voice chant and how the melody slowly rises and falls in waves.

artiest/kate-bush.text:
Kate Bush was born on 30 July 1958 in Bexleyheath, in the south-east of London. She grew up in an artistic family: her father played piano, her mother danced Irish folk dances and her brothers were on the folk scene. At eleven she taught herself to play piano and began writing songs. David Gilmour of Pink Floyd helped pay for a demo, after which she was signed by EMI.

In 1978, aged nineteen, she spent four weeks at number 1 in England with Wuthering Heights, inspired by the novel by Emily Brontë. She was the first woman to reach number 1 there with a song she had written entirely herself. Albums followed such as The Kick Inside (1978), Never for Ever (1980) and Hounds of Love (1985), with hits such as Babooshka and Running Up That Hill. In 1986 she sang the duet Don't Give Up with Peter Gabriel. From The Dreaming (1982) onwards she produced all her albums herself. She often takes years over a record: between The Red Shoes (1993) and Aerial (2005) there were twelve years.

Bush is known for her idiosyncratic style, unusual lyrics and innovative dance on stage. She was one of the first artists to work with the expensive Fairlight sampler. After a tour in 1979 she did not appear on stage again until 2014, with a series of concerts in London. Her sound and her way of moving have influenced many later artists. In 2023 she was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/kate-bush.listen: Listen to Wuthering Heights (1978). Notice the very high voice with which Kate Bush has the ghost of Cathy from Emily Brontë's novel sing, and how the piano carries the song.

artiest/kathleen-hanna.text:
Kathleen Hanna is an American singer and writer, born in 1968 in Portland, Oregon. She became involved in feminism at a young age: as a child her mother took her to a demonstration where Gloria Steinem spoke. As a student at Evergreen State College in Olympia, she founded a feminist art gallery with friends and performed spoken word about sexism and violence against women. The writer Kathy Acker advised her to start a band, because nobody came to spoken word.

In October 1990 Hanna formed the punk band Bikini Kill in Olympia, with drummer Tobi Vail, guitarist Billy Karren and bassist Kathi Wilcox. The band made fast, raw punk and wanted to bring more women into a scene dominated by men. Joan Jett produced the single New Radio/Rebel Girl, and the albums Pussy Whipped (1994) and Reject All American (1996) followed. With members of Bratmobile, Hanna made the fanzine Riot grrrl in 1991, from which a whole movement grew. At concerts she asked women to come to the front, so that they would not be harassed in the mosh pit. After Bikini Kill she made the album Julie Ruin (1997) in her bedroom, with a cheap drum machine. She then founded the electronic punk band Le Tigre in New York.

Hanna gave punk a feminist voice and a way of working of its own: making your own fanzines, playing yourself, teaching each other instruments. Her lyrics were about girls who did and wore what they wanted. The documentary The Punk Singer (2013) tells her story.
artiest/kathleen-hanna.listen: Listen to Rebel Girl by Bikini Kill and notice how Hanna switches between singing and screaming above the heavy drums and guitars. Pay attention to the lyrics too: it is a tribute to another girl, not to a boy.

artiest/katy-perry.text:
Katy Perry's real name is Katheryn Hudson. She was born in 1984 in Santa Barbara, California, the daughter of two pastors in a Pentecostal church. Gospel was mostly played at home; she got to know pop music through CDs that she smuggled in from friends. At sixteen she made a Christian album under her own name, Katy Hudson (2001), which hardly sold. She then moved to Los Angeles, chose her mother's maiden name as her stage name and for years worked with producers and songwriters without a record being released.

In 2007 she signed with Capitol Records. The label put her to work with Dr. Luke, and together they wrote I Kissed a Girl and Hot n Cold. I Kissed a Girl, from the album One of the Boys (2008), spent seven weeks at number 1 in America and also became a number 1 hit in the Netherlands. The disco-tinged Teenage Dream (2010) yielded five American number 1 singles, including California Gurls, Firework and Teenage Dream; no other album by a woman had managed that. Prism (2013) included Roar and Dark Horse. Later albums such as Witness (2017), Smile (2020) and 143 (2024) were less successful.

Perry is a typical product of the hit factory of the 2000s and 2010s. Her songs came about in teams with top producers such as Dr. Luke and Max Martin: short verses, a chorus that sticks immediately and a glossy, hard-hitting production. To this was added an exuberant, colourful image, with costumes and videos that were just as important as the music.
artiest/katy-perry.listen: Listen to I Kissed a Girl and notice the construction: a tight, almost bare verse and then a chorus with hard guitars and a pumping beat. Hear how the chorus revolves around the title phrase, so that you know it after one listen.

artiest/kavinsky.text:
Kavinsky was the stage name of Vincent Belorgey, a French DJ, producer and actor, born in 1975 in Paris, in the Barbès district. According to the source, he died in 2026. His style recalls the electropop of 1980s film music. He said himself that his music was inspired by the thousands of films he watched as a child, whose best parts he brought together in a single concept.

After years as an actor, his musical career began in 2005, encouraged by his friends Jackson Fourgeaud and Quentin Dupieux. He appeared in Dupieux's 2007 film Steak, in which his music was also heard. His first single was Testarossa Autodrive, named after the Ferrari Testarossa. He signed with Record Makers and released three EPs: Teddy Boy (2006), 1986 (2007) and Nightcall (2010), the last with Lovefoxxx of CSS. In 2007 he toured with Daft Punk and Justice, among others. SebastiAn's remix of Testarossa Autodrive appears in the video games Grand Theft Auto IV and Gran Turismo 5 Prologue.

Nightcall became a big success when it accompanied the opening titles of the film Drive in 2011. His debut album OutRun appeared in 2013, followed after seven years of silence by Reborn in 2022. At the closing ceremony of the Olympic Games in Paris in 2024 he played Nightcall with Phoenix and Angèle. He is compared to Daft Punk and Danger. His music made the synthesizer atmosphere of the 1980s popular again.
artiest/kavinsky.listen: Listen to Nightcall and notice the low, distorted voice and the pulsing synthesizer bass: can you feel the night-time drive from the film, and what does the melody do in the chorus?

artiest/kayak.text:
Kayak was a Dutch rock band that was formed in Hilversum in 1972 by Ton Scherpenzeel and Pim Koopman. In 1973 the debut album See See the Sun appeared, with three hit singles. The band's popularity remained mostly limited to the Netherlands. Their biggest hit, Ruthless Queen, reached sixth place in the Dutch charts in March 1979. In 1982 they split up, after nine albums.

On the first five albums Max Werner sang lead vocals. In 1978 he moved to the drums. Ton Scherpenzeel is the only member who plays on every Kayak album. He plays keyboards, accordion and sometimes bass guitar and double bass. The guitar work was in the hands of Johan Slager until 1982. Among other things, the band made Royal Bed Bouncer (1975), The Last Encore (1976), Starlight Dancer (1977), Phantom of the Night (1978), Periscope Life (1980) and Merlin (1981). Phantom of the Night is the best-selling album. The original bassist Cees van Leeuwen left in 1975 to study. He became a lawyer and in 2002 State Secretary for Culture and Media.

In 1999 the band appeared on the television programme De Vrienden van Amstel Live. They then decided to get back together. They released another nine studio albums and three live albums, beginning with Close to the Fire (2000). Kayak is thus one of the longest-surviving names in Dutch symphonic pop, with keyboards as the binding force.
artiest/kayak.listen: Listen to Ruthless Queen by Kayak. Notice the role of the keyboards alongside the guitar and how the vocals float over the whole.

artiest/kayhan-kalhor.text:
Kayhan Kalhor is an Iranian Kurdish kamancheh and setar player and composer, born in 1964 in Kermanshah. He began music at the age of seven and at thirteen was already playing in the National Orchestra of Iranian radio and television. He studied in the Iranian radif tradition and travelled to the north of Khorasan province to study folk music there. Four years after he left Iran, his parents and brother were killed in an Iraqi missile attack during the war between Iran and Iraq.

Kalhor is open to many influences and plays several instruments, but his heart lies with the kamancheh, a bowed instrument with an intense sound. In his playing he often connects the structures of Iranian classical music with the rich folk modes and melodies of the Kurdish tradition. His albums include Scattering Stars Like Dust (1998), Night Silence Desert (2000), In the Mirror of the Sky (2004), Silent City (2008), I Will Not Stand Alone (2012) and It's Still Autumn (2019). He received three Grammy nominations for Best Traditional World Music Album. As a member of the Silk Road Ensemble he won a Grammy for Best Global Music Album.

In 2014 he played a long improvised version of I Will Not Stand Alone in London with the santur player Ali Bahrami Fard, in which plucked and bowed passages alternated. In this way Kalhor brings the old music of Iran and the Kurdish regions to an audience across the world.
artiest/kayhan-kalhor.listen: Listen to I Will Not Stand Alone. Notice how the kamancheh acquires a singing, almost human voice and how plucked and bowed passages alternate.

artiest/kayhan-kalhor-en-mohammad-reza-s.text:
Kayhan Kalhor is an Iranian musician who plays the kamancheh, a bowed instrument with a round resonating body. Mohammad-Reza Shajarian was an Iranian singer and ostad, master, of traditional Persian music. He was born in 1940 in Mashhad, the son of a Qur'an reciter, and began vocal technique at the age of five, at first through Qur'an recitation. At twelve, without his father's permission, he began on the radif, the classical Persian repertoire. He began his career in 1959 at Radio Khorasan and broke through in the 1960s with his own vocal style. He died in 2020.

After the revolution of 1979, Shajarian was one of the few singers who could continue to perform in public. He was known for his mastery of the difficult dastgah style and also sang songs from Mazandarani, Azeri, Kurdish and Luri music. He worked with Hossein Alizadeh, Parviz Meshkatian and Dariush Pirniakan, among others. UNESCO gave him the Picasso Award in 1999 and the Mozart Medal in 2006. The Los Angeles Times called him in 2017 the greatest living master of Persian classical music. After he supported the Green Movement and criticised the government, he was banned from concerts and releases.

Together with Kalhor he made Silence of the Night in 2000, among other things. The duo stands for a music in which voice and bowed instrument follow and challenge each other, in long, free improvisations within a dastgah. In this way Shajarian brought the Persian tradition to a broad international audience.
artiest/kayhan-kalhor-en-mohammad-reza-s.listen: Listen to Silence of the Night and notice the conversation between voice and kamancheh: how does the instrument answer the singer, and how does the melody expand without a fixed rhythm?

artiest/keith-emerson.text:
Keith Emerson was an English keyboardist and composer. He was born in 1944 in Todmorden and grew up in Sussex. He took classical piano lessons, but as a teenager chose jazz piano and also listened to boogie-woogie and rock 'n' roll. After hearing the jazz organist Jack McDuff, he bought his first Hammond organ. In 1967 he founded The Nice. That band became known for rock arrangements of classical music and for Emerson's wild performances: he hit his organ, tipped it over and stuck knives between the keys to make notes sustain.

In 1970 he formed the group Emerson, Lake & Palmer with bassist and singer Greg Lake, who came from King Crimson, and drummer Carl Palmer. The trio broke through at the Isle of Wight Festival of 1970 and became one of the best-known progressive rock bands of the 1970s. Emerson wrote and arranged a large part of the music, on albums such as Tarkus (1971), Pictures at an Exhibition, an adaptation of Mussorgsky, and Brain Salad Surgery (1973). He combined his own pieces with work by Bach, Bartók and Copland. After ELP he made solo records and film music, including for Inferno (1980) and Nighthawks (1981).

Emerson was the first to go on tour with a Moog synthesizer. His modular Moog was three metres high and needed four roadies, and the oscillators went out of tune with changes in temperature. Even so, he made the instrument a permanent part of rock. He died in 2016. He is regarded as one of the technically strongest keyboardists in the history of rock.
artiest/keith-emerson.listen: Listen to Lucky Man by Emerson, Lake & Palmer and wait for the end: there Emerson takes over with a gliding, sharp Moog solo. Hear how that electronic sound stands out against the quiet acoustic ballad before it.

artiest/keith-forsey.text:
Keith Forsey is an English drummer, producer and songwriter, born in 1948 in London. He began as a drummer in the 1960s and in the 1970s worked mainly in Germany. He played in Udo Lindenberg's Panik Orchester, played percussion for Amon Düül II and was one of the busiest session drummers in the country. In this way he ended up in the circle around the Munich disco producer Giorgio Moroder. He played on records by Donna Summer, including Bad Girls, on No. 1 in Heaven by Sparks and on Call Me by Blondie. He also contributed to the early albums of Boney M.

Under Moroder's influence, Forsey began experimenting with electronics and European dance rhythms himself. His solo album Dynamite (1981) was not a success, but as a producer he quickly broke through. In 1982 he produced Billy Idol's debut album and Icehouse's Primitive Man. On Idol's Rebel Yell (1983) he blended synthesizer pop with punk and heavy guitars. With Moroder and Irene Cara he wrote Flashdance... What a Feeling, which won an Oscar in 1984. He then co-wrote The Heat Is On for Beverly Hills Cop and the title song of The NeverEnding Story.

His best-known song is Don't You (Forget About Me) from the film The Breakfast Club (1985). It was offered to several artists before Simple Minds recorded it and had a worldwide hit with it. Forsey shows how the disco studios of Munich shaped the pop production of the 1980s: tight rhythms, synthesizers and a powerful, radio-friendly sound.
artiest/keith-forsey.listen: Listen to I Feel Love by Donna Summer and notice the bass drum: it hits tightly on every beat, and it was played by Keith Forsey. Hear how that human rhythm coincides with the electronic bass line pulsing around it.

artiest/keith-jarrett.text: Keith Jarrett, from Allentown, Pennsylvania, was a child prodigy at the piano and later named Bill Evans as one of his models. He played with Art Blakey, Charles Lloyd and Miles Davis. At ECM he recorded solo records from 1971 and, from 1973, solo concerts that were entirely improvised. The concert at the Cologne Opera on 24 January 1975, organised by the seventeen-year-old Vera Brandes, was played on a poor grand piano; Jarrett therefore stayed in the middle register and with repeated figures. The Köln Concert became the best-selling solo album in jazz. He led an American and a European quartet, with Jan Garbarek, and from 1983 the Standards Trio. After two strokes in 2018 he can no longer play.
artiest/keith-jarrett.listen: Listen to how a repeated left hand forms the basis for a long improvisation.

artiest/keith-jarrett-european-quartet.text:
Keith Jarrett's European Quartet was a jazz quartet with the pianist Keith Jarrett, the saxophonist Jan Garbarek, bassist Palle Danielsson and drummer Jon Christensen. The band came about in the 1970s, after Jarrett had left his esteemed American quartet for a new group of Norwegians and Swedes. The jazz world was surprised and a little sceptical. Even so, according to the critic Ted Gioia, this group made some of the most successful music of Jarrett's career.

The first album was Belonging (1974) and the second My Song, recorded in November 1977 and released in June 1978 on ECM. Jarrett wrote all six pieces. According to the review site AllMusic, they are relaxed and introspective, but full of inner tension. The title track My Song became very popular and made the record the best-known collaboration between Jarrett and Garbarek. The piece The Journey Home shows how wide-ranging the music could be. It begins melancholy and free in tempo, moves into a cheerful, folk-like melody with a danceable beat and ends in a slow section in 9/8.

The quartet's sound is known as looser and more unpredictable than that of the American group. Many critics still praise that freedom today more than the tighter music of the American group.
artiest/keith-jarrett-european-quartet.listen: Listen to My Song by the European Quartet. Notice how Garbarek's saxophone sings the melody and how Jarrett's piano accompanies it quietly.

artiest/keith-moon.text:
Keith Moon was the drummer of The Who. He was born in 1946 in London and grew up in Wembley. As a boy he was restless and full of imagination, with a fondness for explosions and pranks. He learned to drum in a music shop on his way home from school and took lessons from Carlo Little, one of the hardest-hitting drummers of the time. He loved the jazz drummer Gene Krupa, surf music and The Beach Boys. In 1964, aged seventeen, he auditioned for The Who and almost smashed the drum kit to pieces in the process. He was allowed to stay.

Moon played differently from other rock drummers. He did not keep the beat strictly, but filled the songs with rolls across the toms and crashes on the cymbals, in places where nobody else would put them. Bassist John Entwistle said that he played zigzagging across his drum kit. His kit grew ever larger, and together with Ginger Baker he was one of the first rock drummers with two bass drums. He found drum solos boring. On Who's Next (1971) he had to play tightly to a synthesizer part, and according to his biographer that produced his best work. His only solo record was Two Sides of the Moon (1975).

Besides the music, Moon was known for his destructiveness. He kicked over his drum kit at the end of concerts, wrecked hotel rooms and earned the nickname Moon the Loon. He drank heavily and died in 1978, aged 32, of an overdose of a medication for alcohol withdrawal. Many drummers cite him as a model, because he showed that the drums in a rock band can do more than keep time.
artiest/keith-moon.listen: Listen to Won't Get Fooled Again by The Who and notice how Moon comes back after the long synthesizer passage with an enormous roll. In the rest of the song, notice how he almost never simply plays the beat, but keeps throwing rolls and cymbal crashes in between the vocals.

artiest/keith-richards.text:
Keith Richards is guitarist, songwriter and singer of The Rolling Stones. He was born in 1943 in Dartford, in the county of Kent. His grandfather, who toured England with a jazz big band, gave him his first guitar. Richards listened to Billie Holiday and Louis Armstrong, and later to Scotty Moore, Elvis's guitarist, and Chuck Berry, whose solos he learned to play for the most part. On a station platform he met his former schoolmate Mick Jagger again, with records by Chuck Berry and Muddy Waters under his arm. Together with Brian Jones they started The Rolling Stones in 1962.

At the insistence of manager Andrew Loog Oldham, Jagger and Richards began writing songs themselves from 1963. In 1965 came (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction, their first international number 1. According to Richards, the riff came to him in his sleep; he woke up just long enough to record it on a cassette recorder. From Aftermath (1966) the Stones' albums consisted mainly of their own work. Richards also sings himself, for example on Happy (1972), and made solo records such as Talk Is Cheap (1988) and Crosseyed Heart (2015).

Richards does not look for fast solos; his playing revolves around chords and rhythm. In the late 1960s he discovered open G tuning, in which he removes the lowest string and plays on five strings. That sound can be heard in Honky Tonk Women, Brown Sugar and Start Me Up. According to band members, the group does not follow the drummer, but Richards. His partnership with Jagger is among the most successful in pop history.
artiest/keith-richards.listen: Listen to (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction and notice the guitar riff: Richards plays it through a Maestro Fuzz-Tone, which makes the guitar sound like a rasping horn. Hear how that short riff carries the whole song.

artiest/keith-sweat.text:
Keith Sweat is an American singer, producer and songwriter, born in 1961 in Harlem, New York. His mother worked as a hairdresser and his father in a factory. After his father's death in 1973, his mother raised the five children alone. As a boy he performed in the nearby Apollo Theater. Before releasing a solo album, he worked as a night warehouse worker at Macy's and in the mail room of a stockbroker, and earned a communications degree at the City College of New York. Later he even worked on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange.

His musical career began in 1975 with the Harlem band Jamilah. In 1984 he left the group for a solo career and sang in nightclubs, after which he recorded two songs for the label Stadium Records. His breakthrough came with Make It Last Forever in 1987, with hits such as I Want Her. Later came I'll Give All My Love to You, Make You Sweat, Get Up on It, Twisted and Nobody, among others. He released thirteen solo albums, two of them with the R&B supergroup LSG, and discovered the groups Silk and Kut Klose.

Sweat was an early name in new jack swing, the style that combined R&B with the hard rhythms of hip hop. According to the source, his sound was influenced by Steve Arrington of Slave and by go-go. His soft, pleading vocals over tight drum-machine rhythms became the model for much R&B of the late 1980s and early 1990s.
artiest/keith-sweat.listen: Listen to I Want Her and notice the drum machine: how do the hard, tight rhythm beats contrast with Sweat's soft, pleading vocals?

artiest/kelly-clarkson.text:
Kelly Clarkson is an American singer, born in 1982 in Fort Worth, Texas. She grew up in Burleson and was discovered by the choir director of her school, who heard her singing in the corridor. After high school she turned down music scholarships, tried her luck in Los Angeles and returned to Texas after a fire in her apartment. In 2002, on the advice of friends, she took part in the first season of American Idol, and she won.

Immediately afterwards A Moment Like This was released, which became the best-selling single of 2002 in America. Her debut album Thankful (2003) had influences of R&B and gospel. Clarkson then wanted to get away from her talent-show image. For Breakaway (2004) she chose a sturdier pop rock and co-wrote with songwriters such as Kara DioGuardi, Dr. Luke and Max Martin. The album yielded Since U Been Gone, Behind These Hazel Eyes and Because of You; the last of these, about her parents' divorce, reached number 1 in the Netherlands. The dark My December (2007) received a lukewarm reception, but with All I Ever Wanted (2009) and Stronger (2011) she returned to radio-friendly pop rock.

Clarkson is known for her powerful, agile voice. She showed that the winner of a talent show could build a real career, and she remained successful in pop, country and Christmas music. Her collaboration with the producers of the hit factory made Breakaway an example of the pop rock that ruled the radio in the mid-2000s.
artiest/kelly-clarkson.listen: Listen to Since U Been Gone and notice the contrast: the verses are calm and restrained, with a lightly plucked guitar, and then the chorus breaks loose with hard guitars and a soaring voice. Hear how that transition from soft to hard gives the song its power.

artiest/kendrick-lamar.text:
Kendrick Lamar is an American rapper and songwriter, born in 1987 in Compton, a suburb of Los Angeles. He grew up in poverty, in a neighbourhood where gangs called the shots. At school he was a quiet, good pupil. A teacher introduced him to poetry, and through rhyme, metaphors and double meanings he discovered how to write raps. As a teenager he called himself K.Dot and made mixtapes. In 2005 he signed with the independent label Top Dawg Entertainment.

His debut album Section.80 (2011) attracted the attention of Dr. Dre. Then came good kid, m.A.A.d city (2012), a concept album about his youth in Compton, with characters and storylines as in a film. To Pimp a Butterfly (2015) went further still: with musicians such as Thundercat and Terrace Martin he blended hip hop with jazz, funk, soul and spoken word, and he rapped about racism, African American culture and his own depression. DAMN. (2017), Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers (2022) and GNX (2024), with the hit Not Like Us, followed.

Lamar is known for his conscious, personal lyrics and his narrative style. He changes voice and tempo, and slips into the skin of different characters. To Pimp a Butterfly brought a new generation of jazz musicians from Los Angeles to the attention of a large audience. For DAMN. he received the Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2018, as the first musician outside classical music and jazz to do so.
artiest/kendrick-lamar.listen: Listen to Alright from To Pimp a Butterfly and notice how Lamar switches tone and tempo, from frantic to relaxed. Hear how the chorus, we gon' be alright, sounds like a slogan you can shout along to.

artiest/kenji-kawai.text: Kenji Kawai (born in 1957 in Tokyo) first studied nuclear engineering and received almost no formal musical training; he began in the fusion band Muse. His regular collaboration with the director Mamoru Oshii began with The Red Spectacles (1987), followed by the Patlabor films. For Ghost in the Shell (1995) he wrote Making of Cyborg: a song for women's choir in old Japanese, with harmonies that recall Bulgarian folk singing, over heavy drums and echoing synthesizers. That sound became a model for later cyberpunk films and anime. Kawai works in many genres: the horror film Ringu (1998) and Hong Kong action films such as Ip Man (2008) are also on his list.
artiest/kenji-kawai.listen: Listen to the abrasive harmonies in the choir, the ritual drums and the spacious reverb of the synthesizers.

artiest/kenneth-gamble.text:
Kenneth Gamble was born in 1943 in Philadelphia and, together with Leon Huff, born in 1942 in Camden, New Jersey, forms the songwriting and producing duo Gamble and Huff. They are regarded as the creators of Philadelphia soul, the Philly sound of the 1970s. As a boy Gamble recorded himself in recording booths in amusement arcades, helped the DJs of the WDAS morning programme, ran a record shop and sang with The Romeos. At seventeen he was discovered by Jerry Ross. In 1964 he worked for the first time with the keyboardist Huff, on a recording by Candy and The Kisses.

Their first top 5 hit came in 1967 with Expressway to Your Heart by The Soul Survivors. In 1968 they wrote and produced Cowboys to Girls for The Intruders on their own label. They also worked with Wilson Pickett, Dusty Springfield, Archie Bell and the Drells and Jerry Butler. In 1971 they founded Philadelphia International Records, as a rival to Berry Gordy and Motown. CBS Records under Clive Davis supported the label. With the arrangers Thom Bell, Bobby Martin and Norman Harris they made a large part of the most popular soul hits of the 1970s. Almost all the records came from the in-house studio band MFSB, which in 1974 reached number one with TSOP (The Sound of Philadelphia). That song is known as the theme tune of Soul Train.

The Philadelphia sound developed from simple arrangements in the late 1960s into lush strings, driving bass lines and gliding hi-hat rhythms. Those elements became the hallmarks of disco. Gamble and Huff wrote and produced 175 gold and platinum records and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2008.
artiest/kenneth-gamble.listen: Listen to TSOP (The Sound of Philadelphia) by MFSB. Notice the strings, the driving bass and the gliding hi-hat, the ingredients of the Philly sound and of later disco.

artiest/kenny-clarke.text: Drummer Kenny Clarke, from Pittsburgh, led the house band of Minton's Playhouse in Harlem in the early 1940s. He moved the beat from the bass drum to the ride cymbal and used the bass drum and the snare drum for unexpected accents, which musicians called 'bombs'. That earned him the nickname 'Klook'. That became the basis of modern jazz drumming. He played with Dizzy Gillespie and from 1952 to 1955 was the first drummer of the Modern Jazz Quartet. In 1956 he settled in Paris, where he played with European and American musicians and led a big band with the Belgian pianist Francy Boland. He died in 1985 near Paris.
artiest/kenny-clarke.listen: Listen to the cymbal ticking steadily on, with the unexpected hits of the bass drum beneath it.

artiest/kenny-dorham.text:
Kenny Dorham, in full McKinley Howard Dorham, was an American jazz trumpeter, composer and occasional singer. He was born in 1924 in Fairfield, Texas, and died in 1972 of a kidney disease, aged 48. As a child he learned piano, and at high school saxophone and trumpet. He studied chemistry and physics at Wiley College, joined the army and then moved to Los Angeles to become a musician.

Dorham was one of the most active bebop trumpeters. He played in the big bands of Lionel Hampton, Billy Eckstine, Dizzy Gillespie and Mercer Ellington and, from December 1948, in Charlie Parker's quintet. He was one of the first members of the Jazz Messengers. As a sideman he recorded with Thelonious Monk and Sonny Rollins, and after the death of Clifford Brown in 1956 he took his place in Max Roach's quintet. In 1963 he brought the 26-year-old tenor saxophonist Joe Henderson into his group. Out of that came the album Una Mas, among other things. In the 1960s he recorded a great deal for Blue Note and Prestige, also as a sideman for Jackie McLean, Andrew Hill and Milt Jackson, among others.

Dorham also wrote the bossa nova jazz standard Blue Bossa, which was first recorded by Joe Henderson. Critics and colleagues often praised his talent, but the jazz world never gave him the attention many of his contemporaries received. The writer Gary Giddins said that his name has become almost synonymous with underrated. That makes him one of the great forgotten names of bebop and hard bop.
artiest/kenny-dorham.listen: Listen to Blue Bossa in a version by Joe Henderson or Kenny Dorham. Notice the Latin American rhythm and the wistful minor-key melody, over which the soloists build their own lines.

artiest/kenny-g.text: Kenneth Gorelick, from Seattle, began playing saxophone as a child; Grover Washington Jr. became his great model. He played in Barry White's band and in Jeff Lorber's group. His album Duotones (1986), with the instrumental Songbird, was a million-selling success. Breathless (1992) became the best-selling instrumental album of all time. His soprano saxophone sounds soft and smooth, with long sustained notes. Jazz musicians and critics criticised him fiercely, especially after he had his saxophone sound over a recording by Louis Armstrong in 1999. Even so, he reached a larger audience than almost any jazz musician.
artiest/kenny-g.listen: Listen to the long, smooth notes: every note is polished.

artiest/kenny-kirkland.text:
Kenny Kirkland was an American jazz pianist and keyboardist, born in 1955 in Brooklyn and died in 1998. He first sat at a piano at the age of six. After years of Catholic schooling he studied classical piano, music theory and composition at the Manhattan School of Music. His first professional work was a European tour in 1977 with the Polish fusion violinist Michał Urbaniak. He then played with the bassist Miroslav Vitouš, on the ECM albums First Meeting and Miroslav Vitous Group.

In 1980, during a tour of Japan with Terumasa Hino, he met the trumpeter Wynton Marsalis. That was the beginning of a long collaboration with Wynton and his older brother Branford. On Wynton's debut album he shared the piano part with Herbie Hancock, one of his great models. On Think of One, Hot House Flowers and Black Codes (From the Underground) he was the only pianist. In 1985, together with Branford, he joined the Blue Turtles, the jazz-pop band that Sting put together for his solo work. They can be heard on The Dream of the Blue Turtles and Bring On the Night.

After Wynton's band, Branford was his most important partner. In 1986 he became a founder of Branford's quartet and played on the album Buckshot Lefonque. When Branford became bandleader of The Tonight Show with Jay Leno, Kirkland became the pianist of that band. His own album Kenny Kirkland appeared in 1991. He shows how a classically trained pianist could connect jazz, pop and television.
artiest/kenny-kirkland.listen: Listen to a track from Sting's The Dream of the Blue Turtles. Notice Kirkland's piano part and how jazz-like chords and solos fit into a pop song.

artiest/kenny-loggins.text:
Kenny Loggins is an American singer, songwriter and guitarist, born in 1948 in Everett, Washington. He grew up in Alhambra, California, and sang there in the band The Second Helping. In 1970 he was introduced to Jim Messina, who had previously played in Poco and Buffalo Springfield. Messina wanted to help him as a producer, but ended up contributing so much to the first album that a duo came about: Loggins and Messina. The album Sittin' In found its audience in 1972, especially on university campuses. Until 1977 they made seven albums. On them Loggins played rhythm guitar and harmonica and Messina lead guitar, mandolin and dobro.

His first solo album, Celebrate Me Home, appeared in 1977. Nightwatch (1978) contained Whenever I Call You Friend, a duet with Stevie Nicks. With Michael McDonald he wrote What a Fool Believes. The Doobie Brothers' version reached number one and earned both of them the Grammy for Song of the Year in 1980.

In the 1980s Loggins became known as the king of the film soundtrack. He sang I'm Alright for Caddyshack, Footloose and I'm Free (Heaven Helps the Man) for Footloose, and Danger Zone for Top Gun. Footloose, his only solo number one, earned him an Oscar nomination. Later he made Leap of Faith (1991) and the children's album Return to Pooh Corner (1994), among others. He shows how a songwriter from the soft rock of the 1970s could build a second career in film.
artiest/kenny-loggins.listen: Listen to Footloose by Kenny Loggins. Notice the sturdy, danceable drum beat and how the vocals directly follow the movement in the lyrics.

artiest/kent-nagano.text:
Kent Nagano is an American conductor and opera director, born in 1951 in Berkeley. He is a third-generation Japanese American and grew up in Morro Bay, California, where he learned to play piano, viola and clarinet. He studied sociology and music in Santa Cruz and then music in San Francisco, and took lessons at the École Normale de Musique in Paris. His first conducting job was with the Opera Company of Boston. In 1978 he became conductor of the Berkeley Symphony. There he championed the music of Olivier Messiaen, with whom he corresponded and later worked in Paris on his opera Saint François d'Assise.

In 1983 he conducted the London Symphony Orchestra in a number of fully orchestral works by Frank Zappa, who chose him personally. They appeared on the album London Symphony Orchestra, Vol. I. Nagano called that his first real breakthrough. In 1984 he stepped in unannounced and without rehearsal for Seiji Ozawa at the Boston Symphony Orchestra. From 1988 to 1998 he was music director of the Opéra National de Lyon and from 1992 to 1999 principal conductor of the Hallé Orchestra in Manchester. The Deutsches Symphonie-Orchester Berlin, the Los Angeles Opera and later Montreal and Munich followed. From 2015 to 2025 he was general music director of the Hamburg State Opera.

Nagano is known for his inventive programming, especially in chamber music, and for his commitment to new music. He conducted the world premiere of John Adams's The Death of Klinghoffer in Brussels and in 2000 the premiere of Kaija Saariaho's L'amour de loin in Salzburg. In this way he brings the classical concert hall into contact with new work, and with popular music too.
artiest/kent-nagano.listen: Listen to one of the Zappa pieces on London Symphony Orchestra, Vol. I. Notice how a large orchestra plays music that comes from a rock musician, with sharp rhythms and unexpected turns.

artiest/kesha.text:
Kesha Rose Sebert, written Ke$ha until 2014, is an American singer, rapper and songwriter, born in 1987 in Los Angeles. Her mother Pebe Sebert is a singer-songwriter who wrote, among other things, a song that made Dolly Parton famous. In 1991 the family moved to Nashville. As a child Kesha went along to recording studios and wrote songs with her mother. At seventeen she left school when Max Martin persuaded her to return to Los Angeles to make music. She turned down a scholarship to Barnard College.

With Animal (2010) she reached number one in the American album chart, with the singles Tik Tok and Your Love Is My Drug. Warrior (2012) followed with Die Young and later Rainbow (2017), which also reached number one, and High Road (2020). We R Who We R and Timber with Pitbull also reached the top of the Hot 100. Between Warrior and Rainbow her career stood still because of a legal dispute with her former producer Dr. Luke, whom she accused of abuse in 2014. The case was settled out of court in 2023.

Kesha also wrote songs for others, such as Till the World Ends for Britney Spears, and for Ariana Grande and Miley Cyrus. Billboard ranked her 26th among the best artists of the 2010s. She grew into one of the recognisable pop stars of her time, with a mix of singing and rapping, an idiosyncratic style and lyrics that she writes herself.
artiest/kesha.listen: Listen to Tik Tok by Kesha. Notice how she half raps and half sings over a tight dance production, and how the lyrics sound almost like spoken-word chanting.
